newsitem.title: JAPAN: March JGB futures end softer in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: March JGB futures end softer in Tokyo.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended lower in Tokyo trading on Tuesday.
The March contract closed down 0.10 at 126.18, after moving between 126.10 and 126.55. The volume was 44,811 contracts.
The March rose to an afternoon high of 126.40 following Tokyo stock market's sharp slide.
"JGB futures rose following the Nikkei 225 average's fall, but dipped into negative territory by the close as the stock index managed to erase much of its loss," said a brokerage house trader.
The Nikkei 225 average closed down 44.13 points at 20,630.56, off its intraday low of 20,478.74.
In the Tokyo stock market, bank stocks fell sharply after Standard & Poor's Corp said the possibility is high that several second-tier regional banks will go under in the future, traders said.
"S&P remarks were bullish for bonds, but the direct impact on the JGB market was limited, as stocks bounced from lows," said a trader at another brokerage house.
The results of the 1.2 percent four-year JGB auction announced in the afternoon were weaker than expected.
The four-year auction produced a lowest price of 99.76. Traders had forecast a lowest price of around 99.85 to 99.90.
Regional investors and some agricultural financial institutions were the main buyers, traders said.
Despite today's slide, JGB futures looked well-supported, trader said.
"Buying emerged in the March contract at around 126.10. After a short period of consolidation, March is likely to head higher," the first trader said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.370 percent, up from 2.350 percent on Monday.
Earlier in the day, the 182nd JGB yield fell as low as 2.330 percent, the lowest level for any benchmark cash JGB.
Cash JGBs softened slightly following release of Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) data for the July-September period, which came out after the futures market closed.
Real GDP grew 0.4 percent on an annualised basis. The average forecast was for an annualised decline of 0.2 percent.

The stronger-than-expected GDP data for the July-September period is likely to be dismissed by the market as old data, as players are more interested in the economic outlook for next year, traders said.
Some small-lot buying in the 10-year JGBs was evident in the afternoon, a brokerage house trader said. --- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
